summary: Provides encapsulation formats and semantics for emulating SONET/SDH circuits and services over MPLS, letting traditional telephone-style optical circuits travel across a packet network.

eli5.summary: Old phone-company optical links send data on fixed circuits. This explains how to imitate such a circuit across a modern packet network.

what is sonet sdh circuit emulation over packet
what is explicit pointer adjustment relay
subtitle: How to carry SONET/SDH optical circuits across an MPLS packet network as pseudowires.

tldr.problem: Carriers run circuits on SONET/SDH, which sends a fixed-rate byte stream with strict timing, and they want to carry those circuits across a packet-switched network instead.
tldr.mechanism: CEP cuts the SONET/SDH payload (an SPE or VT) into fragments and prepends a CEP header and an optional RTP header. The packets travel over MPLS, and the receiver plays the bytes out at a fixed rate through a jitter buffer.
tldr.outcome: CEP also defines how alarms, pointer adjustments and performance counters map across the pseudowire, plus optional ways to save bandwidth and an LDP signaling extension.

today: RFC 4842 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2007, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Emulating SONET/SDH Over MPLS
sections.content:
RFC 4842 provides encapsulation formats and semantics for emulating Synchronous Optical Network / Synchronous Digital Hierarchy (SONET/SDH) circuits and services over MPLS. The generic framework for this is Pseudowire Emulation Edge-to-Edge (PWE3), described in RFC 3916 and RFC 3985, with extra requirements for TDM in RFC 4197.

Two families of signals are covered. The first is the Synchronous Payload Envelope (SPE) or Virtual Container (VC-n): STS-1/VC-3, STS-3c/VC-4, STS-12c/VC-4-4c, STS-48c/VC-4-16c, STS-192c/VC-4-64c and so on. The second is the Virtual Tributary (VT) or VC-n: VT1.5/VC-11, VT2/VC-12, VT3 and VT6/VC-2. The RFC calls these constructs SONET/SDH channels. Only MPLS packet-switched networks are in scope.
sections.eli5: Phone companies have special fixed-speed lines. This document says how to pretend to be one of those lines while really sending ordinary packets.

sections.title: The CEP Packet and Header
sections.content:
A CEP packet is the PSN and multiplexing headers, then the CEP header, then an optional RTP header, then the SONET/SDH fragment. Fragments MUST be byte aligned with the SPE or VT, and all CEP SPE implementations MUST support a packet size of 783 bytes. VT implementations MUST support a payload of a full VT super-frame and MAY support 1/2 and 1/4 of one.

The CEP header is two 32-bit words. The first four bits are zero, followed by the L bit (CEP-AIS, a failure was detected on the attachment circuit), R (CEP-RDI, loss of packet synchronization), and N and P (negative and positive pointer adjustment). Then come FRG (set to 0 by the sender), a 6-bit Length and a 16-bit Sequence Number that cycles from 0 to 0xFFFF. The second word holds a reserved field and a 12-bit Structure Pointer.

Length is non-zero only when the CEP header plus RTP header (if used) plus payload is 64 bytes or fewer. The structure pointer gives the offset of the J1 byte (SPE emulation) or V5 byte (VT emulation) in the packet, from 0 to 0xFFE, and is 0xFFF when the packet carries neither.

The RTP header is OPTIONAL and is only a formal reuse of the header format when explicit timing transfer is needed. Version is 2, most other fields are 0, the timestamp clock MUST be 19.44 MHz, and RTP mechanisms such as header extensions, RTCP and SRTP do not apply. Over MPLS, the bottom label in the stack demultiplexes individual CEP channels and the CEP header follows the generic PWE3 control word of RFC 4385.
sections.eli5: Each box gets a label with a counter on it, so the other end can tell if a box got lost or arrived out of order, plus little flags for trouble.

sections.title: Packetizing, Playout and Packet Synchronization
sections.content:
The CEP packetizer takes a fixed-rate byte stream from a SONET/SDH interface and, each time a packet's worth arrives, adds headers and sends it. Because packets for one channel are the same length, they SHOULD be sent at regular intervals. The CEP de-packetizer puts arriving packets in a jitter buffer and plays them out at a fixed rate; the buffer SHOULD be adjustable in length.

The sequence number lets the de-packetizer detect lost and misordered packets (it MUST). It SHOULD play out an all-ones (AIS) pattern in place of a dropped packet and SHOULD re-order late-arriving packets; if it cannot re-order, it MUST drop misordered packets.

Packet synchronization is judged at playout time. A de-packetizer starts out of synchronization and declares it after playing out a configurable number of CEP packets with sequential sequence numbers. If it plays more than a configurable number of consecutive empty packets, it MUST declare a Loss of Packet Synchronization (LOPS) defect. LOPS failure is declared after 2.5 +/- 0.5 seconds of defect and cleared after 10 seconds free of it, and the circuit is down while it is declared.
sections.eli5: The receiving end keeps a small waiting room for boxes so it can hand them out at an even pace. If a box is missing, it hands out a blank placeholder so the line keeps moving.

sections.title: Alarms and Maintenance Signals
sections.content:
SONET/SDH failure indications MUST be carried correctly over the pseudowire, and pseudowire failures MUST be mapped back into SONET/SDH indications. In the SONET/SDH-to-PSN direction, an AIS-P/V condition keeps packets flowing as usual but sets the L bit to 1, and the N and P bits SHOULD both be set to indicate loss of pointer. A circuit is declared unequipped only if the signal label, trace (J1/J2) and tandem connection (N1/N2/Z6) bytes are all zero. During loss of packet synchronization the sender sets the R bit (CEP-RDI).

In the PSN-to-SONET/SDH direction, the de-packetizer plays out AIS-P/V when it receives packets with L set, during loss of packet synchronization, and when it receives packets with both N and P set. It sends an unequipped indication when a payload-suppressed packet arrives with L clear, or when the circuit has been de-provisioned.

CEP SHOULD also provide performance monitors. Each second with a missing or dropped packet is an Errored Second (ES-CEP), and each second with a buffer underrun, overrun, LOPS or too many missing packets is a Severely Errored Second (SES-CEP). Unavailable Seconds (UAS-CEP) are declared after a configurable number of consecutive SES-CEP, with a default of 10 seconds. Far-end statistics are based on the R bit.
sections.eli5: If something breaks on the line, the sender raises a flag on every box, and the receiver then shows the same warning light on its own line, so the problem can be traced.

sections.title: Timing and Pointer Management
sections.content:
CEP assumes SONET/SDH transport timing comes either from external sources such as BITS or GPS or from an adaptive timing recovery mechanism, and leaves specific adaptive algorithms out of scope. The wander and jitter limits in G.825 and GR-253 must be maintained.

SONET/SDH pointers slide when two clocks differ. In every case the packetizer MUST include the H3 (or V3) byte in the payload during a negative pointer adjustment and MUST strip the stuff byte during a positive one, and the de-packetizer reverses this.

The OPTIONAL Explicit Pointer Adjustment Relay (EPAR) signals adjustments with the N and P bits, and works only when both ends share a common timing reference. An event MUST be sent in three consecutive packets, and the receiver MUST not replay events more often than once per three packets. For VT emulation, an accumulator converts many small SPE adjustments into fewer VT adjustments, using 783 units as the threshold. The other OPTIONAL method, Adaptive Pointer Management (APM), uses jitter buffer depth to introduce adjustments, and its algorithms are out of scope.
sections.eli5: If the sender's clock and the receiver's clock drift apart, the belt slips a little. CEP either tells the receiver about each slip or lets the receiver guess it from how full its waiting room is.

sections.title: Bandwidth-Saving Payload Options
sections.content:
Beyond pure emulation, CEP offers optional ways to save bandwidth. Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation (DBA) suppresses the payload when the channel is AIS-P/V or unequipped. The Length field then equals the CEP header length plus the RTP header length if used, and padding SHOULD be added if the network has a larger minimum packet size. Implementations that support DBA MUST be able to disable it per channel.

Service-specific payload formats drop parts of the SPE that carry nothing. Fractional STS-1 (VC-3) carries only chosen VTs and can add a 4-byte header word with an Equipped Bit Mask (EBM) of 28 bits, one group of 4 bits per VT group. Asynchronous T3/E3 can drop fixed columns, saving about 7% for T3 (columns 2, 3, 30, 31, 59 and 60) and about 28% for E3 (24 columns of 85). Fractional VC-4 carries selected VCs and can add 12 bytes of EBM words, one 30-bit mask per TUG-3.

Where the path layer is not terminated (LTE implementations), the B3 parity byte has to be compensated so end-to-end parity is preserved, and the egress PE MUST reconstruct the removed unequipped VTs.
sections.eli5: If a box on the belt is empty, there is no need to ship it. These options skip the empty parts, and the receiver puts back placeholders so the order stays right.

sections.title: Signaling CEP Pseudowires With LDP
sections.content:
Using the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) to set up CEP pseudowires, as in RFC 4447, is OPTIONAL. The PW Type MUST be the SONET/SDH CEP type from RFC 4446. The control word is REQUIRED, so the C bit MUST be set; otherwise the pseudowire is not established and a Label Release with an Illegal C bit status code is sent.

Three CEP interface parameters let the two ends check they can interoperate. CEP/TDM Payload Bytes (OPTIONAL) is the expected payload size before any compression, defaulting to 783 bytes for SPE and one super-frame for VT. CEP/TDM Bit Rate (REQUIRED) is in 64-kbps units, for example 26 for VT1.5/VC-11, 35 for VT2/VC-12 and 783*N for STS-Nc. Mismatched rates must be rejected.

CEP Options (REQUIRED) is a 16-bit field with flags for AIS DBA, unequipped DBA, RTP header and EBM extension, a 3-bit CEP Type (0x0 SPE, 0x1 VT, 0x2 fractional SPE), and T3 and E3 bits. A PE that does not support a requested option sends a label release with a CEP/TDM misconfiguration status. Asymmetric configurations, where only one side uses reduction modes, are allowed.
sections.eli5: Before shipping starts, the two ends swap a short checklist: box size, belt speed and which tricks they use. If they do not agree, the line is not opened.

sections.title: Congestion and Security
sections.content:
CEP pseudowires are inelastic constant bit rate flows that cannot respond to congestion in a TCP-friendly way (RFC 2914). They SHOULD be carried across traffic-engineered networks with bandwidth reservation or prioritization. They SHOULD monitor packet loss to detect severe congestion and, if detected, SHOULD shut down bi-directionally. The exact criteria are left for further study.

For security, CEP is subject to the general considerations in RFC 3985, and this document specifies only encapsulations, not the protocols that carry the packets. The security of the emulated service is only as good as the security of the PSN, which may be less rigorous than a native TDM service. SRTP (RFC 3711) is not a substitute for securing the pseudowire and the MPLS network. The RFC adds no IANA requirements.
sections.eli5: The belt cannot slow down when the road is jammed, so it needs a reserved lane. And the delivery is only as safe as the road it travels on.

fields.name: L
fields.desc: CEP-AIS: a failure was detected on the attachment circuit.

fields.name: FRG
fields.desc: Set to 0 by the sender, ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Non-zero only when header, RTP header and payload total 64 bytes or fewer.

fields.name: Structure Pointer
fields.desc: Offset of J1 or V5; 0xFFF when neither is in the packet.
